beats.narration_en: Why is this road spraying water in a snowstorm?
In snowy parts of Japan sprinklers are built right into the street.
Nozzles down the middle of the road spray out water.
It's pumped from deep underground where it stays around fifty degrees.
That's warmer than snow so the snow melts as soon as it lands.
The idea started in the city of Nagaoka in the nineteen sixties.
It works there because the snow falls near freezing so the water doesn't turn to ice.
The catch is it uses lots of water and can make the ground sink.
So newer roads keep the warm water in pipes under the pavement.
That's why some streets in Japan wash their own snow away.
